thirtieth sunday of the year the two great commandments. today’s gospel reminds us of the two great commandments: love of god and love of neighbour. here in a nutshell, we have the whole teaching of the bible. the only real failure for a christian is the failure to love. by rabbinical count, ‘the law’ consisted of some 613 commandments. the question as to which commandment was the greatest was one frequently discussed among the rabbis. jesus was asked to name one, but responded by naming two. that is because, for him, the second followed directly and necessarily from the first. love of neighbour arises out of love of god. both commandments are found in the old testament. what is new is not the fact that jesus brought these two commandments together, but that he made them of equal importance. readings: first reading (ex 22:20-26). god tells the israelites that there must be no discrimination against or exploitation of the weak members of their society . second reading (1 thess 1:5-10). paul encourages the thessalonians by telling them that their exemplary lives have become known far and wide. gospel (mt 22:34-40). jesus tells us that the whole of religion can be summed up in two commandments of love. november dead november is the month of the holy souls – a time when the faithful departed are remembered and prayed for with great intensity. this reminds us of our ongoing connection with those who have gone before us in this life. we are still one family – those on earth, those in heaven and those being purified and awaiting paradise. mass is said each day, in every parish throughout the world for the dead – particularly remembering all those names included on the november remembrance lists. these lists and the november envelopes are available from our remembrance garden. when filled in, these can be put into the redbox. these lists are then placed on the altar of st patrick’s. “in christ the hope of blessed resurrection has dawned, that those saddened by the certainty of dying might be consoled by the promise of immortality to come.” family of parishes there will be an announcement at this weekend’s masses about the diocesan ‘family of parishes’ initiative. we are seeking your views about a potential name for our group of parishes, st patrick’s, holy family and st gerards’s. current options are ‘the cavehill’, ‘ben madigan’ or ‘the trinity’ family of parishes. if you have a preference or alternative, please contact the parish office by phone – 02890 324597 or email –
stpatricks@downandconnor.org

. prayer of the week prayer to st. jude most holy apostle, saint jude thaddeus, friend of jesus, i place myself in your care at this difficult time. help me know that i need not face my troubles alone. please join me in my need, asking god to send me: consolation in my sorrow, courage in my fear, and healing in the midst of my suffering. ask our loving lord to fill me with the grace to accept whatever may lie ahead for me and my loved ones, and to strengthen my faith in god's healing powers. thank you, saint jude thaddeus, for the promise of hope you hold out to all who believe, and inspire me to give this gift of hope to others as it has been given to me. amen thought for the week “don’t let fear haunt your dreams or hold you back from trying something new. sometimes, the scariest steps lead to the most wonderful adventures!” parish collections the offertory collection for sunday 18 october came to £1738.85. dona £170.00. the collection for world mission sunday came to £681.40. dona £75.00. if you wish to donate directly via bank transfer the parish bank details are: account name: st patricks parish account number: 70327727 sort code: 95-06-79 (please add an identifying name to your transaction) or you can contact the parish office for a standing order form. thank you for your continued support and generosity.

sunday gospel true love casts out fear. jesus told his disciples not to be afraid and yet many of those who consider themselves to be followers of jesus are terrified of practically everything that is going on around them. fear paralyses faith, hope and love. nothing will happen in god’s name when believers are afraid of what others think or what might happen. we are called and chosen to love with all our hearts, souls and minds. that teaching is important when the world in which we live is controlled by money, power and wealth. time to wake up to what the lord is teaching. we can change the world if we speak the truth in love and that truth will set us free from the oppression of corruption and evil. (fr s crumptor).
